title: Daily LLM Eval Briefing — 2026-10-12: Self-Scaling Arenas, Perturbation Harnesses, and Domain Benchmark Rigor
subtitle: Same-day arXiv traffic centers on benchmarks that fight leakage, separate transforms from stacks, and replace refusal-only safety scoring with behaviorally grounded protocols.
summary: Coverage for 2026-10-12 is strong: twelve publishable fresh items, dominated by same-day arXiv releases rather than secondary chatter. The clearest evaluation-quality signal is SWE-Duel’s argument that coding arenas should create tasks and oracles at evaluation time so nothing exists in advance to leak, with difficulty set by competing agents instead of a fixed release set. In parallel, perturber packages semantics-preserving text perturbations as a reusable, stateless transform layer so robustness claims can be reproduced outside any one benchmarking stack. DistressBench, GeoFitBench-LLM, a constrained spatial-editing benchmark, GeopoliticalQA, MADS, and a turn-taking speech protocol collectively push evaluation from saturated static scores toward elicitation fidelity, grounded retrieval, adversarial dialogue trajectories, and decision-level conversational behavior. Unsupervised multimodal reward modeling further pressures preference-data assumptions by training a scoring head without human preference labels, using labeled data only for layer selection.
key_takeaways: Treat fixed coding suites as provisional: SWE-Duel’s self-scaling duel design is a concrete anti-contamination pattern—generate tasks and oracles at eval time and let participant strength set difficulty.
Decouple perturbation tooling from leaderboard stacks: perturber’s stateless, identical-across-runs transforms make robustness deltas comparable across labs and CI harnesses.
Safety eval for crisis support must score substantive multi-dimensional help, not refusal accuracy; DistressBench’s 718-conversation design is the day’s clearest construct-validity correction.

New domain benches (GeoFitBench-LLM, constrained spatial editing, GeopoliticalQA) raise the bar on requirements elicitation, geometric constraint satisfaction, and document-grounded RAG—not just answer fluency.
Synthetic adversarial dialogue (MADS) and pause-level speech scoring shift agent eval from function-call accuracy and aggregate latency toward trajectory robustness and human-matched turn decisions.
